title: HiLLM-CD: LLM-Enhanced Hierarchical Cognitive Diagnosis

problem.claim: Cognitive diagnosis aims to infer students' latent proficiencies from their exercise responses.

gap.claim: Existing response-prediction-oriented training can produce less reliable proficiency estimates, while independent concept-wise representations overlook relations among concepts and can yield fragmented and incoherent diagnoses.

contributions.claim: The approach represents each student as an explicit concept tree with node-wise proficiencies.
The concept-tree representation enables coarse-to-fine diagnosis with explicit concept relations.

narrative_sequence.summary: Cognitive diagnosis infers latent student proficiencies from exercise responses.
Response-prediction-oriented training may produce less reliable proficiency estimates.
Independent concept-wise proficiency variables overlook concept relations and may produce fragmented, incoherent diagnoses.
The approach uses explicit concept trees with node-wise proficiencies for coarse-to-fine diagnosis and explicit concept relations.

source_observation.claim: Representing related concepts independently can result in fragmented and incoherent diagnoses.

interpretation.claim: When the target variables have meaningful relational structure, modeling that structure may improve coherence.

application.claim: Consider hierarchical or relational representations for diagnosis tasks involving related concepts.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether hierarchical representation improves outcomes empirically.

unknowns: No datasets, baselines, experimental results, or quantitative comparisons are supplied.
No implementation details or information about how the LLM is used are supplied.
No independent verification or reproducibility evidence is supplied.
